rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to ensure all 8 compounds elute and reveal the overall elution window and any critical pairs. This balances coverage and run time while avoiding an overly shallow method that risks truncation.

The only loss is a single close pair, and all peaks already elute within 10 min, so the next step is to test whether that pair responds to a shallower gradient. Keeping phi0, phi1, and T fixed isolates slope effects by doubling tG.

The critical pair is strongly slope-responsive: tG=20 under-resolves it while tG=40 fully resolves it but is too slow. Try a modestly longer gradient to see if full resolution can be reached while keeping the last peak near 10 min.
The close pair improves as the gradient is lengthened, and 24 min was not enough while 40 min was more than needed. Test an intermediate tG to approach full resolution with a smaller time penalty.

The critical pair is slope-responsive but longer gradients quickly lose too much on time, so test temperature as the next orthogonal lever for selectivity. Lowering T should modestly change selectivity and often improves separation of close pairs, while this broad fast gradient should still keep all compounds observed.

At 25 C only one pair is slightly below full credit, so now optimize the time term by making the gradient a bit steeper while checking whether that near-critical pair stays acceptable. This tests whether we can pull the last peak back toward 10 min without sacrificing much resolution.

The best method is very close to ideal, with one slightly subcritical pair, so probe a small temperature increase to see if selectivity for that pair improves while shortening the run a bit. This is the smallest orthogonal change around the current optimum.

All peaks elute in a narrow mid-range window, so trimming the high-organic end should slightly shallow the effective gradient without lengthening tG, which may push the near-critical pair over 1.5 while keeping t_last close to 10 min. This targets the same selectivity region as the current best but uses the gradient more efficiently.

The narrowed window achieved full resolution but paid too much in time, so shorten tG one step to pull the last peak back toward 10 min while checking whether the critical pair remains above 1.5. This directly exploits the now fully resolved condition.

Further narrowing the gradient window should again shallow the effective slope and may keep the critical pair fully resolved, but with less excess high-organic range than 0.90. This tests whether we can retain full resolution while moving toward a shorter effective elution window.

The first peak is still quite retained, so raising phi0 may trim dead gradient time and reduce t_last without changing conditions near the critical mid-gradient region too drastically. The current best is extremely close to perfect, with only one pair just under 1.5 and t_last only slightly above 10 min. A small increase in tG should push that pair over the threshold while incurring only a modest time penalty, potentially reaching CRF 1.0.

The remaining gap to 1.000 is tiny and seems dominated by a single selectivity-sensitive pair, so try a larger temperature shift than 30 C to see if that pair crosses 1.5 while the slightly shorter retention offsets any time penalty. The 25 C method is already the clear optimum region, so use one injection to bracket the other temperature extreme and rule out any unexpected selectivity reversal that could fully resolve the critical pair with a very short run.
